key_facts: ChatProvider interface: { name: string; chat(messages: ChatMessage[]): Promise<string> }
ChatMessage type: { role: system | user | assistant; content: string }
GroqProvider calls https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions via proxyFetch, model=qwen/qwen3.6-27b, temp=0.7, max_tokens=800
OpenCodeZenProvider calls https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions via proxyFetch, model=big-pickle (configurable via OPENCODE_ZEN_MODEL env), temp=0.7
FallbackChain wraps providers array, returns { result, provider }, tracks fallback counts in fallbacks.json
AiService initializes Groq first, OpenCode Zen as fallback, exposes explain(req) and buildMessages()
AiRequest type: vocabulary | grammar | grammar_auto with selectedText, context, question?, numExamples?, nativeLanguage?, explanationLevel?
3 prompt functions: vocabularyPrompt, grammarPrompt, grammarAutoPrompt - all return ChatMessage[]
stripThinkingTags removes <think>...</think> tags from Qwen model responses
call_chains: AiService.explain(req) -> buildMessages(req) -> vocabularyPrompt/grammarPrompt/grammarAutoPrompt -> FallbackChain.chat(messages) -> GroqProvider.chat() || OpenCodeZenProvider.chat() -> proxyFetch -> HTTP API

data.for_supervisor: VERIFIED: All 4 files read in full. The AI system uses a ChatProvider interface with chat(ChatMessage[]): Promise<string> signature. Groq is primary (model qwen/qwen3.6-27b via Groq API with proxyFetch), OpenCode Zen is fallback (model big-pickle via opencode.ai/zen with proxyFetch). FallbackChain wraps both with retry logic and fallback count tracking. AiService orchestrates via explain(req) method which calls buildMessages then chain.chat. Three prompt types exist: vocabulary (expects JSON response), grammar (free text with user question), grammar_auto (free text, no question). All prompts accept nativeLanguage (default es) and explanationLevel (simple|profound). proxyFetch handles all network calls.
